Subject: Operator entry controls and crypto governance for private deployment

Hi Markus / Lauren,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We're evaluating Redwood for a private VPC deployment and have a few non-standard privacy/compliance asks we need addressed in the DPA and deployment runbook before legal can sign. High level:

- Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) or equivalent where Redwood cannot decrypt customer data; explicit clause that key custody remains with Medisafe.
- Clear operator access boundaries: which Redwood roles (if any) can access customer VMs, logs, or backups; break-glass workflow and justification audit trail.
- List of subprocessors that will touch metadata/logs in the private deployment, and planned geographies for subprocessors.
- Evidence: network flow diagram, SOC2 evidence points (or equivalent), and example audit log export showing operator access records.

I've attached our privacy checklist to show what tags/legal language we expect. Please let me know what you can provide and the timeline — procurement wants this in the next two weeks.

Regards,
Elaine Park
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
Medisafe Inc.

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. We're confident we can cover each bullet for a private VPC or on-prem package. Quick ack and notes:

- CMEK: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments. We normally recommend a KMS integration pattern (Cloud KMS / HSM) where the customer retains control. We'll send a short playbook describing ops demarcation and escrow options.
- Operator access / break-glass: we have a documented break-glass process with time-limited session tokens and mandatory SR/approval. We'll provide an example audit extract.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a current matrix and a process for notifying you of changes (30-day notice for new subprocessors touching logs/metadata).
- Evidence: attaching our initial DPA redlines and a stub network flow diagram; infra will follow up with a detailed diagram and log sample.

Can you confirm whether Medisafe requires cryptographic proof-of-ownership (e.g., signing cert challenge) versus an attestation from your KMS vendor? That affects the playbook we send.

I propose a short 30-minute sync with Legal + Security next Tuesday to walk the redlines and evidence items. Are you available 8/20 at 10am PT?

Thanks — I'll loop Sean for the network/log artifacts.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Markus —
Thanks for the quick reply. A couple clarifications from our side:

- We need cryptographic proof that keys are not exportable from our HSM (FIPS/HSM attestation). A KMS vendor attestation is acceptable if it includes key lifecycle guarantees and export controls.
- For subprocessors, anything that can read unredacted prompts or token-level logs needs to be disclosed. Metadata-only subprocessors are a lower bar but still need categorization.
- Retention: audit/event logs must be retained for a minimum of 13 months and must be exportable in a machine-readable format.

We're available 8/20 10am PT; adding procurement and David (security engineering) to the thread.

Elaine

Hi Elaine, Markus —

Following up from Markus' note. Attached are: 1) a short playbook for customer-managed keys in private deployments (redwood-cmek-playbook.pdf), and 2) our current subprocessor matrix export.

Key points from legal:
- We can accept a DPA addendum that states Redwood will not possess the plaintext key material for customer CMEK; access to model weights or inference state will be encrypted at rest and in transit using keys controlled by Medisafe.
- Break-glass: Redwood may perform emergency operations only with explicit approval from an authorized Medisafe contact or via a documented escalation path; all emergency sessions create immutable audit records and are subject to post-incident review.
- Subprocessor notifications: we can commit to a 30-day notice for changes affecting logs/metadata, and a shorter 7-day notice for critical security subprocessors if feasible.
- Cross-border transfers: for private deployments we will not route customer data to other jurisdictions unless explicitly requested/approved. If some subprocessors operate in other regions, we'll provide a map and legal basis for transfers.

Attachments: redwood-cmek-playbook.pdf, subprocessor_matrix.csv

Please review the proposed language in section 3 (CMEK custody) and section 7 (operator access) — I highlighted the lines where we'd need Medisafe's sign-off or alternate wording.

If that looks good, we'll convert the redlines into an addendum draft and route for signature (DocuSign).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel (Privacy & Security), Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
